source.title: Ecological and social pressures interfere with homeostatic sleep regulation in the wild

confidence_rationale: High-quality field study using accelerometry on wild baboons, and the single most direct literature evidence available that PLACE -- specifically the unfamiliarity of the sleep site -- is an independent input to sleep expression that can override homeostatic pressure. That is the exact functional role MECH-286's threat conjunct is named for. Held below 0.75 because the paper is behavioural rather than mechanistic: it demonstrates that place modulates sleep without identifying the signal that carries place safety, so it establishes the FUNCTION MECH-492 says is unserved without speaking to the sourcing defect itself.
failure_signatures: Sleep expression varied with location novelty in the ABSENCE of any injury, so a place-safety gate sourced from tissue damage would be blind to the entire effect this study measures.

The reduced sleep near unfamiliar locations was NOT followed by compensatory recovery sleep, indicating the place term dominates rather than merely biasing the homeostatic drive -- consistent with MECH-492's framing of the threat conjunct as a hard AND term whose miscalibration is consequential rather than cosmetic.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Sleep in wild baboons, measured by accelerometry, is not governed by homeostatic pressure alone. Ecological and social pressures interfere with homeostatic sleep regulation: animals reduced sleep when at unfamiliar sleep locations, and did so WITHOUT subsequent compensatory recovery sleep.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-286's sleep-onset gate is a three-way conjunction in which one conjunct, threat_ok, is intended to withhold sleep permission when the agent's location is unsafe. Loftus et al. establish that this functional role is real and non-redundant in a biological sleeper: place -- operationalised as location unfamiliarity -- is an independent determinant of sleep expression that can override the homeostatic drive, in animals with no injury of any kind. That is the strongest available literature support for MECH-492's implicit premise that a sleep-permission gate NEEDS a genuine place-safety input, and correspondingly that a term which measures at chance against ground-truth hazard (V3-EXQ-950: AUC 0.5016 damage_sourced, 0.4966 proximity_ema_sourced) leaves the gate unable to perform the function it is named for. The absence of compensatory rebound also speaks to MECH-492's consequence leg: in biology the place term is a hard constraint on sleep, not a soft bias, which is the regime in which a degraded conjunct matters most.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The paper measures location UNFAMILIARITY, not location HAZARD, and those are distinct constructs -- an unfamiliar site may be safer than a familiar one. MECH-492's falsifier is defined against ground-truth hazard, so this is an adjacent rather than identical operationalisation. More importantly, the study is purely behavioural: it demonstrates that place modulates sleep but says nothing about WHICH neural signal carries place safety, and therefore cannot arbitrate the sourcing question (damage_sourced vs proximity_ema_sourced) that is MECH-492's actual subject. It also cannot speak to the 0.4 threshold or to conjunctive degradation. Baboon-to-artificial-agent transfer is long, and the social pressures the study also identifies have no REE analogue at all, so only the ecological half of the finding maps.
mapping.source_context: Wild olive baboons (Papio anubis), Mpala Research Centre, Kenya; tri-axial accelerometry collars with simultaneous GPS on a whole troop; naturalistic sleep-site use over multiple nights including familiar and unfamiliar roosting locations.

confidence_components.notes: eLife; well-powered field accelerometry on a wild troop with simultaneous positional data -- strong for an ecological study, though observational rather than manipulative, so the place-to-sleep link is correlational. Mapping fidelity moderate: the functional role maps cleanly, the operationalisation (unfamiliarity vs hazard) does not quite. Transfer risk moderate-to-high: primate field behaviour to an artificial sleep-onset gate, and only the ecological half of the paper's finding has any REE analogue.
